newsitem.title: INDIA: India's monsoon rains seen normal in 1997.
newsitem.headline: India's monsoon rains seen normal in 1997.

text.p: India's annual monsoon rains, crucial to farm production and the health of the overall economy, are likely to be normal for the 10th successive year in 1997, the Meteorological Department said on Sunday.
The department said in a statement that nine of 16 measures used to predict the monsoon were favourable and "there is a very good probability of a normal monsoon this year".

The southwest monsoon rains usually strike the southwestern tip of the subcontinent around June 1, and move progressively north, eventually covering the entire country before tapering off in September.

"In 1997, the southwest monsoon rainfall over the country is likely to be normal,...thus making the year 1997 the 10th normal monsoon year in succession," the department said, adding that normal was defined as rainfall within 10 percent of the long-term average.
It said the monsoon rains were expected to hit the southern state of Kerala a few days after the normal arrival date of June 1.

In much of India, the southwest monsoon provides most of the annual rainfall. India's economy remains primarily agriculture-based, and adequate rainfall can bolster farm production, add to national income and keep down prices.
